findings.summary: Workflow-level concurrency gate (Holder::Run) is never released when a run terminates through the dependency-skip/eval-error arm of promote_ready_jobs. A successor submission to the same group without cancel-in-progress parks in `pending` forever.
evidence: promote_ready_jobs Skip|Error arm (runtime_scheduling.rs:862-879) sets terminal status + finalize_run_if_complete but never calls release_concurrency_for_run
release_concurrency_for_run has exactly one production caller: cancel_run_inner (runtime_scheduling.rs:151)
finalize_run_if_complete (runtime_scheduling.rs:2027-2041) only stamps completed_at/conclusion, no release
try_acquire_concurrency (runtime_scheduling.rs:595): a dead Holder::Run blocks the group; only the cancel_in_progress arm evicts it (cancel_holder -> cancel_run_inner -> release)
TLC counterexample: SubmitRun2(run1,{job1}) -> EnqueuePending -> ArriveRunFree(run1,g2) -> SkipJob; run terminal StSuccess with holderKeys[run1] = {g2}

findings.summary: Job-level concurrency gate (queued_job.concurrency) is evaluated only at submit time and only for needs-empty jobs; jobs with needs (or max-parallel violations) carry their gate through pending_jobs and are dispatched by promote_ready_jobs without ever acquiring it.
evidence: try_enqueue_with_job_concurrency has exactly one production call site: runs.rs:1077, guarded by `needs_empty && under_mp` (runs.rs:1099-1121)
needs-gated jobs go to inner.pending_jobs (runs.rs:1118) with concurrency field set
promote_ready_jobs Run arm (runtime_scheduling.rs:850-857) pushes directly to inner.queue without consulting queued_job.concurrency
TLC counterexample: SubmitRun2(run1,{job1}) -> DeclareGate(run1,job1,g1) -> EnqueuePending -> PromoteDispatchJob; job dispatched while gateHeld = {}

findings.summary: ServerQueue.take_steps_update_body clears dirty_keys while steps_generation stays ahead of published_generation; a failed POST (flush_step_updates publish=false) never re-dirties the steps, so the next take returns an empty body and the terminal step transition is lost forever.
evidence: take_steps_update_body (server_queue.rs) returns None only when generations match, otherwise collects dirty_keys and clears them
flush_step_updates (reporting.rs:19-77) calls mark_steps_published only when the POST/PATCH succeeded; on failure neither re-dirties nor restores
a step in terminal state receives no further queue_update, so nothing re-registers it as dirty
TLC counterexample: WorkerQueueUpdate(st1,StCancelled,RNone) -> WorkerTakeBody; gen != pubGen with dirty = {}

findings.summary: The aksh-gha-protocol copy of the template-string builder (azdo/job.rs template_string_token) escapes only single quotes; the parser copy (job_builder.rs append_format_literal) also escapes { and }. The official runner's format() throws FormatException on unescaped braces, so any env/input mixing a literal brace with a ${{ }} expression breaks on dispatch through the protocol (AzDO/broker) serialization path.
evidence: protocol copy: azdo/job.rs:588-615 template_string_token escapes only `'` (literal.replace('\'', "''"))
protocol copy is live: TaskStep::serialize -> TemplateStringMap -> TemplateStringMapPair::serialize -> template_string_token (azdo/job.rs:312-319, 555-585)
official runner Format.EvaluateCore throws ExpressionResources.InvalidFormatString for lone { or } (runner v2.336.0 src/Sdk/DTExpressions2/Expressions2/Sdk/Functions/Format.cs:20-85)
TLC counterexample: SetEscapeBraces(FALSE) -> BuildFormat(TRUE,TRUE); formatError set
